newsitem.title: UK: OPTIONS - Weak UK stock market attracts FTSE trades.
newsitem.headline: OPTIONS - Weak UK stock market attracts FTSE trades.

text.p: With the feeble state of the London stock market on Friday most of the action in equity options were volatility trades in the FTSE 100 index options and futures, dealers said.
One large deal was to buy 1,500 June 4225 calls in the FTSE at 71p, against selling September futures at 3882.
In general, an increase in implied volatility of the market will help this strategy make a profit by September expiry because that would increase the call premium.
Another trader took the opposite view on volatility and sold 750 lots calls in the same series at 71p against buying futures.
By 1445 GMT, the cash FTSE index was 18.6 points weaker at 3866.4 while September futures were 15 down at 3879.
In stock options, the main trade in supermarket chain Safeway was a split synthetic long position established by buying 500 October 360 calls at 5p and selling 500 October 330 puts at 5p.
Safeway shares were unchanged at 341-1/2p and the options position will make money at expiry if the shares go above 360p.
In British Petroleum a calendar spread was the biggest deal involving the sale of 500 October 600 puts at 6p and the purchase of 500 April 600 puts at 22p.
BP shares lost 1-1/2p to 619p and for maximum profit at October expiry the shares need to fall to 600p.
The April puts will still be held if the holder believes the shares will drop further between the October and April expiry.

Over in retailer Marks & Spencer the chief trade was a short straddle which was the result of the sale of 500 January 500 puts and calls at 21p and 18p each. The deal will make 39p profit at expiry if the shares are the 500p.
M & S shares were unchanged at 492-1/2p.
